hook: There is a version of you that doesn't negotiate with himself. He's not a different man.
body:
**There is a version of you that doesn't negotiate. Doesn't stall. Doesn't need a reason to do what he said he'd do.**

You know this version. You've been him before — for a week, maybe two. When everything lined up and you were operating close to what you know you're capable of.

That man is not a different personality. He is not a product of better circumstances. He is you, operating with a working system instead of an absent one.

The difference between that version and the version who negotiates every morning is not character. It is architecture. The negotiating version has no pre-decided rules. Every decision is made fresh, in the moment, by whoever he happens to be that morning.

And whoever he happens to be that morning is often not the man who made the commitment. He's tired. He's comfortable. He has reasons.

The non-negotiating version already decided. There is no morning negotiation because the decision was made in advance, in a clear state, and it does not reopen.

You don't need to become someone else. You need to stop making the same decisions twice.
